title: Wiring
note: One USB-C port for charging and data: VBUS charges the cell through the TP4056 and runs the unit through the load-sharing switch; D+ and D- go to the Pico's USB test pads. The MT3608 makes about 5.2 V from the cell, and a 1N5822 joins it to the Pico's VSYS, so it can never push power back into a computer. Dashed parts are wired in on their leads and are not in the 3D model.

groups.label: Load sharing: USB runs the unit while the cell charges
groups.note: With USB in, Q2's gate is at 5 V and it is off: the MT3608 runs from VBUS through D2, and the TP4056 sees only the cell, so it ends the charge properly. With USB out, R4 pulls the gate low and Q2 connects the cell.

components.name: USB-C breakout
components.note: The only USB port on the unit. CC1 and CC2 each have a 5.1 k resistor to GND on the board, so a USB-C charger supplies 5 V; SBU1 and SBU2 are not used.

components.name: TP4056
components.note: 1 A single-cell charger with protection (DW01 + 8205A). Its own USB-C port is not used: power comes in on IN+ and IN-. IN- and OUT- are joined on the board.
One 18650 cell in its holder, glued to the floor.

components.name: 1S BMS
components.note: Mantech 210454 protection strip, on the cell. A second layer of protection in series with the TP4056's own; it can be left out.

components.name: AO3401 P-FET
components.note: Any small P-channel MOSFET with a gate threshold under about 1.5 V (AO3401, SOT-23).

components.name: 22k
components.note: Holds Q2's gate low with USB out. 22 k rather than 100 k, so the Schottky's leakage cannot lift the gate.

components.name: 1N5822
components.note: Feeds the MT3608 from VBUS while USB is in. Same 1N5822 as D1, on its leads.

components.name: MT3608
components.note: Boost converter: set its trimmer for about 5.2 V out before connecting the Pico.

components.name: 1N5822
components.note: Joins the MT3608 to VSYS; the Pico's own diode joins VBUS to VSYS, so whichever is higher runs it, and nothing flows back into the USB port.

components.name: Pico 2 W
components.note: On its side behind the LED stick. USB data reaches it on test pads TP3 (D+) and TP2 (D-) on its underside, so its micro-USB port is not used. It can tell USB is in from VBUS sense (WL_GPIO2 on the Pico 2 W).

components.name: WS2812 x8
components.note: Eight LEDs in the lid's windows; up to about 480 mA at full white. Its data comes straight from the 3.3 V GPIO, which works at this supply in practice.

components.name: TSD-1166
components.note: Push button with a white LED ring, through the back wall. The switch reads on GP3 with the internal pull-up.

components.name: 47R
components.note: Limits the button's LED to a few mA from the 3.3 V GPIO; check against the LED's rating.

components.name: Buzzer 5V
components.note: Active 5 V buzzer, 30 mA: more than a GPIO gives, so Q1 switches it.

components.name: DS18B20
components.note: Measures the air inside the box; one-wire on GP6.

nets.name: VBUS
nets.note: 5 V from the USB-C port. It charges the cell, feeds the Pico (through its own diode) and, through D2, the MT3608; it also turns Q2 off.

nets.name: GND
nets.note: The protected side of the TP4056 (IN- and OUT-, joined on its board). Never join it to B- or the cell's negative.

nets.name: PACK-
nets.note: Through the BMS strip's MOSFETs. Leave the strip out and the cell's negative goes straight to the TP4056's B-.

nets.name: SYS_IN
nets.note: The MT3608's input: the cell through Q2, or VBUS through D2.

nets.name: BOOST
nets.note: About 5.2 V, set on the MT3608.

nets.name: VSYS
nets.note: About 4.8 V after the diode: the Pico, the LEDs and the buzzer.

nets.name: RING
nets.note: The button's LED ring: high is on, PWM to dim.
